candidate_relations.label: Listeria Meningitis
candidate_relations.reason: The CSF findings (neutrophilic pleocytosis, positive culture) and clinical context support Listeria infection, but the dominant pathology is rhombencephalitis (brainstem/cerebellar MRI lesions, cranial nerve signs, tetraparesis, Romberg positivity). Meningitis alone does not capture the defining anatomical component.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Listeria etiology confirmed but anatomical specificity missing; meningitis is a component/manifestation but does not capture the brainstem/rhombencephalitis localization

candidate_relations.label: Listeria rhombencephalitis
candidate_relations.reason: The clinical picture—brainstem/cerebellar MRI lesions with ring enhancement, cranial nerve involvement, tetraparesis, neutrophilic CSF pleocytosis with positive culture, foodborne exposure cluster, and MS patient on DMF—is fully consistent with Listeria rhombencephalitis, identical to the reference diagnosis.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Matches etiology (Listeria monocytogenes) and anatomical localization (rhombencephalitis = brainstem/cerebellum) as required by the reference

candidate_relations.label: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML)
candidate_relations.reason: PML is caused by JC virus reactivation and typically presents with non-enhancing white matter lesions, normal CSF cell count, and no fever or meningismus. This patient has neutrophilic CSF pleocytosis, positive bacterial culture, fever, neck stiffness, and ring-enhancing lesions—all inconsistent with PML.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Different etiology (JC virus vs Listeria) and different clinical/CSF profile

case_quality_flags: CSF culture positivity strongly supports bacterial etiology; organism not explicitly named in record but clinical context (foodborne cluster, immunomodulated MS patient, brainstem predilection) is classic for Listeria monocytogenes
